Privacy Policy

Metre — AR tape measure for iPhone and iPad · Effective date: 21 October 2026

Metre (“the app”) is published by gokchetech (“we”, “us”), an independent iOS developer. Metre was built to work entirely on your device. We do not run any server that receives, stores or analyses your data. This policy explains exactly what the app touches on your iPhone or iPad, and why.

At a glance

  • We collect no personal data through the app. Its App Store privacy label is “Data Not Collected”.
  • Camera frames, photos and 3D scans are processed on your device and never uploaded.
  • No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking, no third-party SDKs.
  • Your measurements stay in the app on your device until you delete them.
  • Purchases are handled by Apple; we never see your payment details.

1. Data we do not collect

We do not collect, receive or store any personal data through Metre. In particular:

  • There are no user accounts. You never sign up, sign in or give us an email address to use the app.
  • Camera images, photos, room scans, measurements and notes are never uploaded to us or to anyone else.
  • The app contains no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising or tracking SDKs, and it does not use the advertising identifier (IDFA). It never asks for permission to track you.
  • We do not sell, rent or share data with third parties, because we have none to share.
  • Metre does not access your location, microphone, contacts or health data.

2. What the app uses on your device, and why

Metre asks for the following permissions through the standard iOS prompts. You can change each of them at any time in iOS Settings → Metre.

  • Camera: to measure with augmented reality. Frames are analysed in real time by Apple’s on-device frameworks (ARKit, Vision and, on LiDAR devices, RoomPlan) to find surfaces, edges, objects and body outlines. Frames are not stored or transmitted, except for the snapshot you choose to save with a measurement.
  • Motion sensors: for the bubble level and plumb, and as part of AR tracking.
  • Photos: when you use Measure a photo or the size estimate from a photo, you pick a single photo with the iOS photo picker; Metre only receives the photo you pick, never your library. When you ask to save an image, Metre adds it to your library and needs no access to read it.

3. Data stored on your device

The things you choose to save stay in the app’s private storage on your device:

  • measurements, their small preview images and notes; projects, home surveys, floor plans and 3D room scans;
  • body measurements and a client measurement book, if you use them, and child height entries;
  • preferences such as units, precision, appearance and screen calibration.

This data is protected by iOS app sandboxing and device encryption. Metre does not sync it to iCloud or to any server. Like any app’s data, it is included in your device backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup) if you have turned those on; Apple handles those backups under its own terms. You can delete individual items in the app, and deleting Metre removes all of its data from the device.

4. Sharing and exports

When you share a result or export a PDF, CSV, DXF or USDZ file, the iOS share sheet sends it only to the destination you choose (for example Messages, Mail or Files). From then on, the recipient’s or service’s own privacy terms apply. Nothing is shared automatically.

5. Widgets and Siri Shortcuts

Metre’s widgets and shortcuts open a measuring tool in the app. They run through iOS, and we receive no information about their use.

6. In-app purchases

Metre Pro subscriptions and the lifetime purchase are processed by Apple through the App Store. We never receive your name, Apple ID, payment card or billing address. The app checks with Apple’s StoreKit on your device whether Pro is unlocked. Apple provides us with aggregated sales reports that do not identify you. Apple’s handling of your purchase is described in the Apple Privacy Policy.

7. Information Apple may share with us

If you have turned on Share with App Developers in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements, Apple may share anonymised crash reports and usage statistics with us. We use them only to fix bugs. You control this setting, and it is off unless you turn it on. The App Store may also ask you to rate the app; ratings and reviews are handled by Apple.

8. Contacting us

If you email us, we receive your email address and whatever you write, and use them only to answer you. Our mailbox is provided by Google (Gmail), which may store messages on servers outside your country. We delete support conversations when they are no longer needed, or sooner if you ask. The legal basis is your request and our legitimate interest in answering it (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b) and (f); KVKK Art. 5(2)(c) and (f)).

9. Children

Metre is a general-audience utility. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone, including children, because the app collects none. The child height tracker is meant for parents and its entries never leave the device.

10. Your rights (GDPR, UK GDPR, KVKK, CCPA)

Depending on where you live, you have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict or port your personal data, to object to its processing, and to withdraw consent. Under the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK), Article 11 gives you equivalent rights, including the right to learn whether your data is processed.

Because Metre keeps your data only on your device, you exercise most of these rights directly: view, edit, export or delete your measurements in the app, or delete the app to remove everything. For support emails, write to us and we will answer within 30 days. You also have the right to complain to your data protection authority, for example your EU member state’s supervisory authority or, in Türkiye, the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK).

We do not sell or share personal information as defined by the California Consumer Privacy Act.

11. Data controller

gokchetech, independent iOS developer. Contact: sengulfaruk1@gmail.com.

12. Changes to this policy

If we change this policy, the new version will be published at this address with a new effective date. If a change affects how data is handled, we will also say so in the app’s release notes before it takes effect.
